name: Investor introduction
description: Cold outreach to investors. Leads with a number, not a narrative, because that is the only thing that separates you from the other two hundred messages this week. Never asks for money in the first touch.
audience: Partners and principals at funds whose stage and thesis actually match where you are. Ten to forty names, researched individually.

variants: {{firstName|Hi}} — building in a space {{company|your fund}} has written about. Not raising this minute; connecting now so I'm not a stranger when we are.
Hi {{firstName|there}} — your thesis lines up with what we're building. Happy to connect and keep you posted rather than appear mid-round.

Thanks {{firstName|there}}. Short version: we've gone from nothing to a real revenue line in twelve months, growing month on month, mostly inbound. Would an update every quarter be useful, or is that noise?
Context in three lines, {{firstName|there}}: twelve months old, revenue compounding monthly, distribution is our moat and our weakness. Happy to send a quarterly note if that's welcome.
{{firstName|Hi}} — we'll open a round in the next couple of quarters. Rather than pitch you cold then, would half an hour now be worth it to you?
No ask today, {{firstName|there}}. When we do raise I'd like you to already know the numbers. Half an hour in the diary at some point?
I'll stop here, {{firstName|there}}. Adding you to the quarterly update — one email, easy to unsubscribe from.
Leaving it there, {{firstName|there}}. I'll send the quarterly note and nothing else. Good luck with the current book.
